photos.c: The above photograph was taken last January, on a ramble which started from Faygate,Sussex and shows Barry Sawyer, Ron 'Ozog' Langheim,Derek Crookes Mike Shingles, Chris Steer, and Bob Taylor.
TOP LEFT Chris Steer, Mike Shingles, Bob Taylor and Barry Sawyer on one of their Sunday rambles.
The National Brighton Relay of 1954. Bob clocks fastest time on the present Stage 10

Bill Aylett of Blackheath was a noted contemporary of Bob Taylor. They are seen here during two half-mile races in 1953. LEFT: Taylor (10) is dogged by Aylett (4) in the L.C.C. Champs. The Blackheath man pipped Bob for the title in 1:55.6.
RIGHT:Bob gains his revenge in the Surrey v. Middx. v. Kent match, where he beats Aylett (Kent) and Martin (Surrey) in 1:58.9.
Above: Bob Taylor, Doug Briggs and George Stace during a training session at Tooting Bec track.
My picture shows Bill (far right) alongside Chris Steer, our President Bob Taylor, Trevor Hart and Alan Black; with the two Norths and Dabbs in the front row.
Frank Jarvis presents the retiring President's plaque to Bob Taylor.

Above: The 70s and a photo call after a Young Athletes Sunday morning training session at Wimbledon Park. The adults, left of the group, left to right are: John Martin, Frank Simmons, Jim Heathfield (crouching), Bob Taylor, Reg. Hopkins Jnr., Reg Hopkins Snr. And on the right: John Baker, Philip Gee, Peter Hilliar, Gordon Biscoe, Mickey Pyer, Gordon Doubleday, Alan Mead and Bill Couzens.

Left: Part of the Belgrave T&F Team of '67 pose with President Frank Jarvis at the end of a successful season.
Back row: Brian King (throws), Chris Keavey (middle distance), Bill Couzens (throws), Don McLean (middle-distance and steeplechase), Frank Jarvis, Nick Head (javelin), Bob Taylor (Team Manager), Bill Dance (middle distance), Adrian Major (middle distance), Alan Black (middle-distance and steeplechase).
Front: John Mitchell (long jump and sprints), Phil Smith sprints John Martin (throws), Tony Brooks (440/880), Alan Mead 440/880).
